items.title: Lionel Reason Interview, 1981-05-26
items.q: And I had met Louis Armstrong in New Orleans, but he didn't know too much about me.

ctx.x: Good, and my name is Dick Allen. We've got a directional mic there, so we have to check and see if it'll pick up everybody else. I understand. Yeah. Well, anyway, I wanted to ask you a lot of questions about Paul Barnes, nicknamed Polo, because you've already been interviewed before by a lot of other things. And I went through his journal.

When did you first meet Paul? I met Paul in 1929 in New Iberia, Louisiana. I was playing with a band under the leadership of Beauregard Adams, an alto player. And the name of the band was the Nighthawks, a six-piece band. And during that time, times were pretty tough. So we were working on these $2, $2.50, $3.00 night jobs. And I had been with them about a year. And I knew the whole territory by going around with this little band. And, in fact, I came to New Iberia on a freight train. It was during the…
Oh yeah, I know him. Well, they had a band.

items.title: Lionel Reason Interview, 1981-05-26
items.q: I was, if there had been things that had been improved, I was going back to New Orleans. So he told me, he said, well, you will be the last of the New Orleans musicians I'll ever send for.

ctx.x: Right after I came out of the Army. I went back to Detroit. Then I came back to New Orleans in 1948. The latter part of 48. And, uh, uh, uh, uh, with, uh, with Joe, it, it, it, it just seem as if he, as if he had just said, well, just let it all go. Mm-hmm. And, uh, it wasn't good for his business. Wasn't good for his business. And, uh, he was having trouble with his stomach. And that was because of, uh, he had bad teeth. Mm-hmm. And Louis gave him the money three times to have his teeth fixed. The king would not…
Did he have trouble with his lip much in those times?
